deadly traps...? The stairwell, from
which you can return to the upper floor
of the castle, is to the north, while a
massive steel door leads through the
wall to the west.

224.text: You look around the dungeon master Kay's room. Everything in this room uncomfortably reminds you of that nasty B-class movie you saw at your home cinema last month: a movie about people being held captive in his dungeons by a cruel despot until they became too weak so that they could still beg for mercy or even scream for help during the long and disgusting torture procedure that awaited them! Kay and his sidekick Kriss seemed to have been similar sadists: all over the room you will find instruments of torture whose meaning and purpose would be far beyond your innocent imagination! Each of the devices is lovingly explained, such as "Thumbscrews for FLAKE fingers", "For our dear Holger", or "Dahmlos'sche Jungfrau". In another corner of the room hangs a cage in which two rotten skeletons crouch, benevolently to be described as human: "The Seifert team: Mr. Copper & Blitter-Boy" is written in delicate letters on the board next to it. You think of the poor creatures who, no doubt involuntarily, had to give this instrument of torture its name: apparently they were the unfortunate knights who dared to defy Zargon's will... The only way out of this site of hundreds of murders is through a small latticed door in the South.

225.text: You are in the basement of the stairwell. "Hmmm...: It's pretty dark down here!" You recognize with an expert eye, since you can hardly see anything (man! What a sentence!). The passage leads north into a corridor, east into an armory, and south into the gatekeeper's office.

In the corner stands a life-size statue of a seasoned ancient warrior in full armour. You can only leave the armory through the west door, which leads back into the stairwell.

227.text: You enter a gloomy hall. Yes, really: Unfortunately I really can't tell you much more about this: You are standing in a very simple tunnel whose only function is to connect two rooms with each other, since we had to "build them around the corner". You understand what I mean? Yes? Guy! Of course you do NOT understand it, because you certainly didn't draw a map for yourself, did you? see! I hope that you can still forgive us for this emergency solution, because after all you made it this far without any notable (Yes: NOTICEABLE! If you knew what awaits you here...!) problems and therefore probably some, hopefully fun hours spent in our little world, right? So, and after all this incoherent nonsense, with which we have once again managed to put together a multi-line room description, here is a brief summary of what we came up with in three years of development to describe this location. So: To the right on the wall next to you there is a curtain behind which lies the passage to the castle's wine cellar, and further north you can see an eerie, phosphorescent glow. Scary, huh? I mean: Scary how you can pack so little information into so much dull text!

228.text: You are standing in a damp wine cellar below the pantry. The heavy smell of fermentation in the air almost takes your breath away: It doesn't matter what noble drops may have once been in the three huge wooden barrels that are leaning against the western wall: In WINZER the stuff that is probably completely fermented these barrels wouldn't even win a flowerpot anymore! However, one of the barrels looks pretty familiar to you - you just can't seem to remember where you might have seen it before... Via the slippery stone steps in the north-east corner of the cellar vault you get back to the pantry on the ground floor of thecastle.

229.text: You enter a corridor in the basement of the castle. Right in front of you rises a huge black ebony door, eerily bathed in the glow of torches mounted on the walls. Oddly enough, the otherwise untreated, rocky ground one meter in front of the door is neatly tiled: this is where the living quarters seem to start again. Now you can either go back to the stone steps in the south or try to open the door in the north - if it isn't already open... As you happen to look up, you see two dirty gray birds in the blue sky high above your head circling: "Vultures!", it instinctively shoots through your head... You must have a quirk! We are several meters underground! Maybe you should just stop taking those dreadful drugs?

230.text: You enter a long, gloomy hall lined with some mysterious stone boxes. Exactly in the middle of the vault someone has drawn a large pentagram on the floor. After your eyes have gotten used to the darkness down here, your blood freezes when you look at the large containers again! These "boxes" are somehow too big and massive for ordinary chests or the like! They can only be... COFFINS! You break out in a cold sweat of fear: "NO! Please, not again!" You fervently beg the A.C.A gods - but they show no mercy: These boxes are and will remain coffins! And now you finally notice the penetrating smell of rot and decay in the air - the sweet scent of death, which oozes out of every crack in the stone sarcophagi in thick, light green clouds of smoke... The only visible way out of this room is the portal in the south , which will lead you back to the lobby.

232.text: If you are interested in Spiritism, the occult and similarly obscure things, you had better save your progress now and open your teepee in this black library - you would feel like in seventh heaven! The bookshelves on the walls are literally bending under the weight of the old, yellowed rinds: Here you can read about everything that a confused mind has ever thought up and put on paper on the subject of devil worship, death cults and other absurdities. Aside from the shelves, the rest of the library's furniture consists of a large antique leather armchair that stands in the center of the room and a matching study table from which a candle set in a cracked human skull dominates the room immersed in its erratic, flickering light... Exits lead in all four directions - you may just have to find them first...

237.text: You are in the gatekeeper's house. Like all other servants at the king's court, he seems to have been a butah dwarf, which can be easily seen from the size of his small wooden hut: when you enter it you have to bend low to avoid banging your head on the door frame to bump! The tinyness of the furniture confirms your assumptions: Even the relatively generously sized bed would be too small for you to be able to sit on it even halfway comfortably! Otherwise, however, the entire living space is quite sparsely furnished, albeit not nearly as primitive as the other rooms in this cave system might lead one to expect. Through the small door in the north wall you can get back to the shore of the small island.

Leaning casually against a rough-hewn counter and contentedly chewing on the mouthpiece of his pipe, you can see the ferry captain: an old, white-bearded sea dog with a blue captain's hat on his head. You can exit the ferry house through the door in the eastern wall.

to escape from this ominous wall at the
very last second, before the gate has

late: it falls with a loud bang massive

Well, you're probably up to your neck in

249.text: It seems the rats don't have quite as much time to waste as you do, because it's supper time and the fat beasts seem to know it perfectly well: as if on cue, they all jump at you at once! You can hardly resist the stubborn attacks of the little beasts and you are thrown to the ground, where you have to watch helplessly as you are processed into a tasty rat meal! Well: It's really a pretty bad feeling to have an eye ripped out of your head while you're still alive: the pain almost drives you insane! But just as you open your mouth to roar loudly, a rat jumps onto your face, dances there to hot, ritualistic rhythms - and during a pirouette, tears you into an ecstatic and spirited "Ouh!" tongue out with a flourish so that your scream is muffled by a warm gush of your own blood to a gurgling rattle! Don't worry, you won't choke on it! Because with your remaining eye you can already see a third rat sniffing your carotid artery curiously before it finally cuts it through with a single, hearty bite of its razor-sharp incisors and puts you out of your torment...

However: Somehow our two disguise artists seem to be a bit infantile, because obviously they want to be in front of yours Death play another round of tug of war with you! Well, your body didn't exactly have competition quality, because it tears after only two rounds of dogged back and forth, so that from now on there will probably be two halves of you from which your burst intestines will spill out and the nice, clean floor with it blood and bile defiling...

251.text: When you materialize again in the middle of the white pentagram in Zargon's mystery, the old witch rises from his high chair in amazement. "Why did you have to come so early?", he rasps with a hint of disappointment in his voice, "I don't have any time at the moment to take care of you - unfortunately...!" With a seemingly irrelevant movement of his right hand, he creates a huge fireball in the air out of nowhere and hurls it right at you! The last thing you can think about in the remaining time is Zargon's extreme waste of energy - because a small, subtle flash would probably have done it! Then it suddenly becomes very bright - and very hot! After all, a small pile of smoking ash is all that's left of your body...

252.text: When Zargon sees you appear in the middle of his white chalk pentagram, he gets up and rises to his full height: "Why couldn't you wait?" he snarls in disappointment, "I have absolutely no time for you at the moment - unfortunately..." With a slight flick of his right hand, he attempts to summon a fireball, but all you can see is a small flame scorching his palms! As you giggle gleefully, the sorcerer screams in pain, "Damn! But you haven't won yet!" He claps his hands briefly ("Say hooo!"), and a few seconds later two huge, ugly mummies materialize in the pentagram next to you. Completely shocked and unable to defend themselves, you don't cause them the slightest problem: Strong claws grab your throat, and shortly thereafter you hear your neck with a short but loud "Krack!" break! "Thank God!" You think, still relieved, "I was afraid they would strangle me!" As your soul flees to the Eternal Hunts, you watch as your head is brutally ripped from your torso and smashed to the ground, where your viscous brain mass now swells over the stone slabs until Zargon will have them wiped away...

253.text: Well, if you really think that Zargon should be afraid of you breaking into his secret chambers, then you've got a another thing coming! On the contrary: he calmly finishes his conversation with one of the demon lords and only then turns to you. "Get out of here, let's go!" he shouts at you after looking at you appraisingly for a few seconds, "Do you think I would let you run around in my castle for hours just to follow you around? Let you slaughter me without being able to have a little fun with you first? You have no chance at all of defeating me yet - so get out of here and prepare yourself a little better for our fight! After all, I want to have fun too! A man rarely gets to treat himself to anything else..." With these words he angrily pushes you out the door and closes it behind him. From outside you can hear him muttering indistinctly: "These young fools! They don't have the slightest idea, but they always want to bang their heads against the wall! How does this weirdo think he could ever get a place in the high score list? Me I think I really need to have a serious word with Chris and Kai: It's bad enough to put me in such a stupid game, but then to send such wimps past me - that's really going too far! I should really contact the association against non-player characters -complain about torture..."

255.text: Noticing the Butah King's cloak around your shoulders, the old ferryman falls to his knees and asks in a submissive voice, "Your Majesty wishes to use the boat?" After he has licked your feet clean, the ferry captain goes back to his work with countless bucks. You see: clothes make the man!

261.text: Noticing your intention to enter his lair, the Cu-Sath bares his teeth in anger, but then...: But wait a minute! What is that? It looks like the beast likes your perfume as it's the same one its master used a long, long time ago! You won't believe your eyes when the otherwise dangerous beast begins to purr gently and nestles tenderly against your body! Then you feel something strange, warm running down your calves: Disgusted, you look down your pant leg where the Cu-Sath has left its scent to show you its strong affection. But then you shrug indifferently: After all, being soiled with animal excrement is healthier than being processed into animal excrement, right? Strengthened by the deep philosophical meaning of this knowledge, you continue your way through the cave with a happy heart...

269.text: When Zargon notices you looking around for his soul crystal, he tries to get to the pedestal in front of you - but it is already too late: With two or three light-footed steps you reach the pedestal, grab the jewel and lift it high over your head : The stone pulsates dull in your hands, as if it were filled with life of its own! When he realizes that you have now gained power over him, Zargon resorts to begging: he desperately begs you to spare him, he offers you Mylgor's position as his governor in the small village - yes, he promises to even turn you back into a human if you leave his crystal untouched: He says there is a spring somewhere whose water could heal you of your infection from the werewolf blood.. For a brief moment you ponder what has happened, review your mind's eye and think about what probably weighs more: your fate - or that of the tormented and downtrodden villagers, and it doesn't take you too long to reach a decision: Without paying any more attention to Zargon's whimpering,you smash the Soul Crystal to the ground with all your might, where it shatters into a thousand pieces, each of which s till reflects Zargon's portrait! However, just as the crystal shatters, you hear Zargon screaming hysterically behind you! Scared to death, you turn - to see Zargon in agony with a dense, dark gray cloud, which must have been released by the breaking apart of the Dark Jewel, where it must have waited many decades for this one moment! Only Zargon's wildly flailing arms and legs still peek out of the dirty gray fog! Then - suddenly - the spook is over: the cloud disappears as quickly as it appeared, and with it the evil sorcerer! An oppressive silence fills the room as you let yourself slide down the wall, exhausted: all that is left of Zargon is his crown and the royal scepter...

315.text: As if in a trance, you look up at the pale, full moon - until you are snapped out of your thoughts by a strange noise from the mountain to the north: It is the same noise you heard back then in the overgrown cemetery of the old, dilapidated monastery - only: this time you don't feel afraid anymore - no, on the contrary: the noise even seems to be familiar to you in a very strange way, seems to call you, to entice you...? All of a sudden you feel a burning pain in your chest, as if a dark force wanted to take possession of your body from within! Out of your mind you want to tear your shirt off in pain - and freeze: your chest is covered all over with shaggy black hair, just like your arms - and after a few more agonizing seconds your whole body! You try to scream, but you don't recognize your own voice: instead of a human scream of pain, the sound in your throat is - WOLF HOWL...! Feverishly you try to fight back your panic and to think clearly: Apparently the wound that the werewolf inflicted on you during your midnight duel in the run-down monastery cemetery was not quite as harmless as you initially assumed in your naivety! You could slap yourself in anger, but it's no use... Hoping that King Richard will find a way to heal you once you escape these cursed walls, you decide to think further about your hairy future postponed for now...

At the last moment you grab the edge of the pitfall and try to pull yourself back up: "I wish I hadn't skipped gym class so often!", you think to yourself desperately when, after several futile and exhausting attempts, you realize that you are... you will never be able to free yourself from this predicament without outside help. When you look at the bottom of the pit in a panic, you see long iron spikes deep below you, with remnants of coagulated blood sticking to them! You instinctively want to call for help, but as soon as you open your mouth you realize that your screams would only be a complete waste of energy and time, since the only person who could hear and find you down here would be Zargon himself - and you know very well that he would have no pity on you! So after you have reminded yourself of the hopelessness of your situation, you say one last prayer and then let go of the edge of the pit...
